purpose: Proves a route registered via a "...handlers" spread argument resolves its individual handlers when the spread slice is a literal this analyzer can see in full (inline or a same-function local variable bound to one), and stays honestly unresolved — never silently dropped, never fabricated — for anything else (a function-call result, a keyed/sparse composite).

expectedRoutes.note: Inline []gin.HandlerFunc{A, B}... resolves both handlers in order; B is the final handler.
named := []gin.HandlerFunc{A, B}; r.GET(path, named...) resolves identically to the inline case.

expectedUnresolved.note: dynamicHandlers()'s return value is not a literal; route not inventoried.
A keyed composite literal is not resolved; route not inventoried.
